sentences.text: Revenue, net interest income plus noninterest income, compounded from $96.6 billion in FY2016 to $182 billion in FY2025, a 7.3% CAGR [D5][D206].
The path was a step change, not a smooth compound: revenue was $119.5 billion in FY2020, $121.6 billion in FY2021, then $158 billion in FY2023 and $177.6 billion in FY2024 [X5][X6][X8][X9].
FY2023 revenue rose 22.9% as net interest income climbed 33.8%, with higher rates lifting net interest income [D179][D174][P36].
FY2025 revenue growth slowed to 2.8% as deposit margin compression and lower rates offset higher Markets net interest income and Card revolving balances [D226][P28].
North America remains the core at 76.6% of FY2025 revenue but contributed only 0.2pp of growth, while EMEA added 1.2pp and Asia-Pacific 1.2pp [D249][D251][D276][D301].

FY2025 noninterest income rose 2.4% to $87.0 billion, lifted by Markets revenue, AWM asset management fees and a $588 million First Republic-related gain, offset by the absence of the prior year's $7.9 billion Visa gain [D222][F20][P27].
Noninterest expense grew 4.2% against revenue growth of 2.8%, so the incremental margin was negative in FY2025 [D225][D226].
That expense growth came from higher compensation, brokerage and distribution fees, auto lease depreciation and technology and marketing investment [P26].
Diluted EPS still grew 1.4% while net income fell 2.6%, because the diluted share count shrank 3.4% [D216][D214][D224].
The efficiency ratio was 52.4% in FY2025 against a window median of 57.2%, a low of 51.7% in FY2024 and a high of 59.2% in FY2022 [D207][D333][D331][D332].
That 52.4% sits far below the banks peer median of 61.7% and ranks at the 0th percentile, where a lower ratio is better [D207][D337][D336].
The credit-loss provision rose to 7.8% of revenue in FY2025 from 6.0% in FY2024, above the peer median of 6.0% [D208][D185][D341].
The FY2025 provision reflected net portfolio growth, client-specific credit quality changes, updated loss assumptions on leveraged loans and estimated fraud losses [P15].
Net margin of 31.2% held close to operating profitability, with the effective tax rate at 21.4% [D210][D203].
Operating cash flow is not a meaningful earnings-quality measure for a bank; it swung to -$147.8 billion in FY2025 from -$42.0 billion in FY2024 [F60][F59].
The FY2025 outflow came from higher trading assets, securities borrowed, loan originations held for sale and other assets, partly offset by net income [P21].
Capital return is the better test: buybacks plus dividends of $48.2 billion were 84.6% of FY2025 net income of $57.0 billion [D205][F30].
Return on average equity was 16.1% in FY2025 against a banks peer median of 11.8%, ranking at the 100th percentile [D213][D339][D338].
Loans were 57.3% of deposits, up from 43.1% in FY2021 as deposits grew faster than lending through the pandemic [D211][D115].
FY2025 loans rose $121.1 billion, driven by CIB Markets and AWM securities-based lending on higher client demand [P4].
Buybacks of $31.6 billion and dividends of $16.6 billion in FY2025 exceeded the $48.2 billion combined total of the prior year [X102][X112][D205][D182].
Net income for FY2021 through FY2025 in the table is proxy-sourced and rounded, differing from the 10-K by up to 0.10%; the 10-K figure for FY2025 is $57.0 billion [R1][X20][F30].
The FY2025 provision of 7.8% of revenue is above the 6.0% peer median, and criticized wholesale exposure rose to $48.5 billion from $44.7 billion [D208][D341][P2].
The increase in criticized exposure was driven by SPEs, Consumer & Retail, Banks & Finance Companies, Healthcare and Chemicals & Plastics, mainly from downgrades [P2].
FY2020 pretax income and tax were later restated against the first-reported $35.4 billion and $6.3 billion used here, a data-quality caveat on that year's figures [X63][X73].
If the efficiency ratio rises above the 57.2% window median from 52.4%, the cost advantage would be reversing [D207][D333].
If the credit-loss provision climbs above the FY2020 level of 14.6% of revenue from 7.8%, credit quality would be deteriorating [D208][D88].
If net interest income growth stays below the FY2025 3.1% rate, the rate-driven step change would be fading [D221].
